## The Animator {#the-animator}

**Animate ⏱** opens a resizable dock with a named step strip, millisecond ruler, and timing lanes.
Object and semantic-part names stay readable in the fixed left column, even for short effects.
Select a lane to select and outline its stage target. Hovering a lane outlines the exact object or
plot parts. Selecting an object identifies its effects in the current step.


<figure class="doc-figure"><a href="/assets/media/docs/slides-timeline.png" data-enlarge data-caption="The Animator gives each effect a lane. These six Change tracks share a duration, while their faint curves show different timing."><img src="/assets/media/docs/slides-timeline.png" alt="The native animation timeline, with Linear, Smooth, Enter, Overshoot, Bouncy and Steps lanes." width="1956" height="720" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>The Animator gives each effect a lane. These six Change tracks share a duration, while their faint curves show different timing. Click to enlarge.</figcaption></figure>

To animate something, select it on the stage (**Ctrl+click** drills to a plot part), then use:

- **Appear** / **Ctrl+Shift+A** — add an entrance.
- **Transform ▾** — one action, three ways: **Change** (**Ctrl+Shift+C**) shapes a new state of the
  object at this step; **Ghost…** (**Ctrl+Alt+G**) creates copies that transform independently;
  **Become** (**B**) turns the object into another one. See [Transforms](/docs/transforms.html#transforms).
- **Emphasize** — add a **pulse**, a calm swell and return. **Highlight**, **Dim** and **Circle it**
  are in the Effect menu of the Animation inspector.
- **Disappear** / **Ctrl+Shift+D** — add an exit.
- **Focus** / **Unfocus** — dim everything else, then bring it back. See [Focus on one thing](#focus).

Flux chooses an entrance suited to the object: text, images and plots rise in, shapes and arrows
grow in, and lines and paths draw on. Adding another effect keeps the existing ones. Effects on the
same target start after its existing effects by default.

### Auto-animate a plot {#auto-animate}

**✨ Auto-animate** builds a plot's entrance from its semantic anatomy and the plot's own hints,
in three clicks:

1. **Axes & grid** — the axes and their colour key. Each gridline fades in alongside its own
   axis's ticks, which arrive one by one along the axis.
2. **Data** — lines draw on, bars grow from their baseline, points and hexagons stagger in,
   however many there are. A data line draws **along x**, at an even pace from left to right; its
   confidence band opens behind the same front, its markers grow in as the line reaches each one,
   and a line without markers is led by a small dot. A mean marker draws itself on as its points
   arrive, its error bars grow out of it and their caps close them.
3. **Legend & annotations** — the legend's frame, then its entries, then annotations and
   brackets, each bracket with its own label.

Each click starts after the short delay the plot suggests, and everything the plot draws is part
of the build: nothing sits on the slide before its click. A multi-panel plot offers **panel by
panel**: the same three clicks for each panel in turn (an inset right after its host), with the
figure's title first and its shared legend last. Auto-animate replaces the plot's generated build
and keeps the effects you added by hand. It needs the plot's parts tree, so a plot saved by an old
fluxplot adds nothing until it is regenerated.

The same build is available from the command line and to agents; `--pace classic` keeps the
older timing numbers:

```bash
flux animate-plot talk slide1 plot1 [--per-panel] [--pace classic|v2]
```

<!-- MEDIA: Auto-animate on a line plot with a confidence band and markers: Axes & grid arrive tick by tick, the line draws along x with the band opening behind it and the markers growing in as it reaches them, then the legend and a bracket with its label. -->

### Focus on one thing {#focus}

**Focus** dims everything else on the slide to 30 % at this step, so the selection stands out.
A label inside a selected object, and anything grouped with it, stays bright; a selected object
that an earlier Focus dimmed comes back to full. Objects that are already dimmed, or that play
another appearance in this step, are skipped (Flux lists them), and objects not yet on screen are
left alone. **Unfocus**, on a later step, brings back everything a dim left below full opacity,
smoothly from exactly where it is. Both are ordinary **Dim** and **Highlight** effects collected
in a lane group, so you can retime or remove them like any other effect.

```bash
flux focus talk slide1 step2 plot1 label1 [--level 0.3]
flux unfocus talk slide1 step3
```

<!-- MEDIA: Focus on a slide with a plot and three labels: everything but the chosen label and its box dims to 30 %, then Unfocus on the next step brings the rest back. -->

### Select and arrange effects {#select-and-arrange-effects}

Drag a box from empty grid space to select several effects. **Shift** or **Ctrl/Cmd** adds
to the selection; **Escape** cancels. Click empty space to clear it. Selecting effects does
not change their timing.

| To… | Do this |
|---|---|
| Change when an effect starts | Drag its timing bar |
| Change its duration | Drag the bar’s right edge |
| Reorder lanes | Drag a bar vertically |
| Move an effect to another step | Drag it onto that step; hold **Alt** to copy |
| Select several lanes | **Shift** or **Ctrl/Cmd+click**; **Ctrl/Cmd+A** selects the step’s effects |
| Group or ungroup | **Ctrl/Cmd+G** or **Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+G** |
| Duplicate selected effects | **Ctrl/Cmd+D** |
| Zoom or fit the timeline | **Ctrl/Cmd+wheel** or **fit ⟲** |

<details class="doc-details"><summary>Groups, scrolling and snapping while you drag</summary>

Groups collapse without changing timing. Double-click a group name to rename it; drag its
span to retime or move the whole group. A selection box that crosses a collapsed group
selects its members. Scroll while drawing the box, or hold near the grid edge to scroll.
Right-click a lane for grouping, duplication and moves to named steps.

The ruler and grid fill the visible time axis at every zoom. While you drag, a guide follows
the moving edge. It spans the ruler when the edge snaps to another effect or a grid line.
Every visible major and minor grid line is a snap target; a 50 ms grid also catches drags
between them. Resizing snaps the effect’s end. A single selected effect shows its start and
end across all lanes.

</details>

On macOS, **Alt** is **Option (⌥)**. Focus the Animator before using these keys.

Select effects and press **Alt+A** to align their starts, or **Alt+D** to align their ends.
Their durations stay the same. Add **Shift** to resize instead, keeping the opposite edge fixed.
These actions are also available on a bar’s right-click menu.

Press the shortcut again to try the next alignment:

1. If the selected edges differ, the first press aligns them to their own earliest start or latest end.
2. Later presses use each lane above the selection, nearest first. A guide and ruler label identify the target.
3. After the last choice, the effects return to their original timing. One **Undo** also reverses the entire cycle.

Moving a start detaches its [Follow timing](#follow-timing) link, as dragging does.
A toast names the former source lane.

<details class="doc-details"><summary>Align tracks from the command line or an agent</summary>

`align-tracks` performs the same edit from the CLI and MCP. Name a reference track, or give
an exact time in milliseconds:

```bash
flux align-tracks talk slide1 --tracks e3,e4,e5 --edge end --to rect2
flux align-tracks talk slide1 --tracks e3,e4 --edge start --to 250 --resize
```

See the [slide command reference](/docs/commands.html#slide-commands) for more commands.

</details>

### Inherit an effect's animation {#inherit-an-effects-animation}

Use **Inherit animation** to copy another effect’s settings:

1. Select the effects you want to change.
2. Hold **Ctrl+Alt** (**⌘+⌥** on macOS) and drag a bar onto the source lane.
3. Release when **Inherit from ‹name›** appears. Hold **Shift** as you release to copy the start time too.

A dashed guide identifies the source. Release elsewhere or press **Escape** to cancel;
**Undo** reverses the entire drop. You can also right-click a bar, choose **Inherit animation
from…**, and click the source lane.

Inherit copies the source's duration, easing or spring and stagger. Between two entrances (or two
exits, or two transforms) the effect itself and its options come too — four pops become four
rises. Across kinds only the timing travels, so an exit stays an exit. If the source uses an
[animation style](#animation-styles), the effects link to that style instead and follow its
later edits. What the effects animate, their transform endpoints, links, groups and on/off state
never change. Inherit does not copy timing between video commands and animation effects.
`inherit-track` does the same from the CLI and MCP:

```bash
flux inherit-track talk slide1 --from rect2 --to e3,e4,e5,e6 [--include-start]
```

### Animate plot parts from the X-ray {#animate-from-the-x-ray}

The **X-ray** (**R**) lists a plot's named parts as a tree, and you can animate from it:

1. Select one plot, or several, and press **R**. A multi-plot X-ray lists the parts every
   plot shares. (**Shift+Alt+R** x-rays a drilled part's whole family, such as every tick label.)
2. Pick the rows you want: **Shift+click** a run, **Ctrl/Cmd+click** to toggle a row,
   **Ctrl/Cmd+A** for all.
3. Press **M** and choose **Appear**, **Emphasize**, **Disappear** or **Change** (**5** starts
   **Appear from…** and **6** **Animate like…** from the same rows).

Appear, Emphasize and Disappear give each picked part its own effect on the current step, ready
to retime. **Change** selects the plots that own the parts; edits to part styles are captured in
each plot's Change. Picking the same part through both a common row and its plot's own tree
creates one effect, not two. With **Show hidden** off, parts that have already disappeared are
left untouched by visibility and animation actions on common rows.

### The Animation inspector and keyboard {#the-animation-inspector}

The **Animation** inspector edits the selected effects' target, part, effect, start, duration,
easing, stagger and any effect-specific controls. When the selected effects disagree, a timing
field stays blank until you set one shared value. Choose a new target or part to repair a
missing binding. An issue banner lists missing targets, unmatched parts, unsupported effects and
conflicting overlaps; click an issue to inspect its track. The **Easing** field shows the timing
curve and opens its editor. **Library** holds reusable presets and multi-track templates.

Keyboard commands belong to the focused surface:

- **In the Animator or the Animation inspector**: **Delete** removes effects, the arrow keys move
  between steps and lanes, **Alt+←/→** retimes starts, **Alt+Shift+←/→** adjusts durations, and
  **Alt+A** / **Alt+D** align starts / ends. **P** focuses Effect/Action, **D** Duration,
  **T** Start/Offset, **G** Stagger, and **E** opens Easing.
- **On the canvas**: **Delete** removes objects and the arrow keys move them.
- **In a text field**: keys keep their normal editing behaviour.

**Ctrl/Cmd+Z** undoes one edit or gesture wherever you are.

### Default timing {#default-timing}

New effects are written at a measured pace. Nothing in an existing deck is retimed: an effect
authored before this pace keeps its own numbers, and so does every effect you have edited.

| New effect | Duration | Curve |
|---|---|---|
| Entrances — Fade in, Rise in, Pop in, Stagger in | 0.7 s | Quick smooth |
| Scale in | 0.6 s | Quick smooth |
| Draw on, Wipe in, Grow bars | 0.9 s | Quick smooth |
| Count up | 0.9 s | Smooth |
| Exits — Fade out, Pop out, Scale out, Draw off, Wipe out | 0.5 s | Quick smooth |
| Highlight, Dim | 0.7 s | Quick smooth |
| Pulse | 0.7 s | Smooth |
| Circle it | 0.9 s | Smooth |
| Change, Ghost, Become | 1.2 s | Smooth |
| Camera | 0.9 s | Smooth |

**Quick smooth** is the Smooth S-curve with its slow first moments removed, so a click shows
motion at once. Three rules shape how steps feel in Present and in exported decks:

- An **After previous** step waits 150 ms before it starts.
- A click while an effect is still moving finishes that effect in at most 0.12 s, then starts
  the next step, so a presenter can never outrun a build.
- Selecting three or more objects and choosing **Appear** or **Disappear** lags them in reading
  order, at most one second in all; two objects stay together, and shapes that start together
  grow about their shared centre.

The alignment diagrams above use their own example durations; the rules here only decide what a
*new* effect is given before you touch it.

### Easing and springs {#easing-and-springs}


<div class="doc-study" data-doc-study="/demos/studies/easing.html">
<div class="doc-study-stage"><img src="/demos/studies/easing.svg" alt="Hundreds of spike marks ease into a histogram" width="1280" height="720" loading="lazy"><button class="doc-study-launch" type="button" data-study-start data-title="Hundreds of spike marks ease into a histogram" hidden><span aria-hidden="true">▶</span> Try this example</button></div>
<div class="doc-study-caption"><span class="study-label">Interactive example · a slide from the Flux film</span><p><strong>One easing, hundreds of moves.</strong> Every spike mark travels to its histogram bin with <strong>Smooth</strong> easing: it speeds up, then settles. Because all 346 marks share the curve, the rearrangement reads as one gesture. Simulated spike trains. Use the next-step arrow to play; reset to watch again. Reduced motion shows each finished step.</p></div>
</div>

Select an effect and click **Easing**, or press **E** while the Animator has focus.
The field shows the curve, when the motion first arrives at 90% of its travel, and when it
settles. A faint curve inside each timeline bar shows the same timing; springs also have an
arrival tick.

![The Easing field shows arrival and settle times.](/assets/media/docs/animation-curve-field.png){fig-alt="The Effect section of the Animation inspector. Its Easing field reads Smooth, arrives 452 ms, settles 600 ms."}

Choose a tile from **Ease**, **Overshoot**, **Spring**, or **Discrete**. Hover a tile for one
preview pass; reduced motion keeps that preview still. Focus a group and press **1–9** to
choose within it. **Bouncy** is a spring with overshoot and a settling tail. Adjust
**Bounce** to change its character and **Velocity** to change its starting speed. For a Discrete
curve, **Steps** sets the count from 1 to 60. The **overshoot …%** readout reports how far the
curve passes its endpoint; data and other bounded channels still stay within their limits.

![Bouncy, its spring graph, and the spacing chart.](/assets/media/docs/animation-curve-spring.png){fig-alt="The Easing editor with Ease, Overshoot, Spring and Discrete tile groups. Bouncy is selected; its spring graph, Bounce and Velocity controls, spacing chart and overshoot readout appear below."}

**Keep arrival** starts checked. It adjusts each selected effect's duration to preserve its
arrival time as you change the curve, within 150–4000 ms. A 600 ms Smooth move becomes about
1418 ms with Bouncy: the motion arrives at the same time and the bar grows to hold the settling
tail. Turn Keep arrival off to keep the bar's duration instead. A follower anchored to the bar's
end waits until settling finishes.

The graph's handles edit a custom bezier. Arrow keys move a focused handle by 0.01;
**Shift+arrow** moves it by 0.1. The numeric fields let you enter exact values. Existing
influence curves keep their handles horizontal; dragging vertically converts them to a free
bezier. The spacing chart shows 13 positions at equal times: close dots mean slower motion.

Use the **Paste a curve…** field and **Paste** button, or **Ctrl+V** in the editor, to enter
names such as `bouncy`, `quick smooth` or `glide`, or strings such as
`spring(0.35, v=2)`, `cubic-bezier(.2,1.4,.4,1)` and `steps(8)`. **Copy** copies the current curve.
Invalid text shows an error without changing the effect. Different selected curves show
**Mixed**; choosing a curve applies to all selected effects as one edit. **Enter**, **Done**,
or clicking outside commits; **Esc** restores the opening curve and duration.

**Data never overshoots.** Box movement and camera motion can spring past their destinations;
data values, count-up text, plot views, opacity and reveals stay within their valid range.
**PowerPoint uses Morph's own ease**; Flux's curve is retained in Flux playback and HTML exports.

Right-click a timeline bar and choose **Copy timing**, then select other effects and choose
**Paste timing**. This copies duration, curve and stagger together as one undoable edit.
It leaves their targets, start times and linked style identities in place.

### Animation styles {#animation-styles}

Deck animation styles share an effect's preset, parameters, duration, easing, stagger, arc and
start. A linked effect inherits absent fields; changing a field on that effect overrides the
style for that field. Editing the style updates every inheriting effect. An effect links only to
a style of its own kind (appearance, transform or video command); linking gives it the style's
preset, and changing the style's preset changes it on every linked effect. Detaching a style,
or deleting it, keeps each effect's current settings. Saved slide presets carry the styles
they use, and insertion reuses an existing style with the same name and family.

Select an effect and open **Style ▾** in the Animation inspector. Choose a deck style of the
same family, or **Save as new style…** and enter a name. Selecting several effects links them
all; a selection spanning different families explains why linking is unavailable.

<figure class="doc-figure"><a href="/assets/media/docs/animation-style-picker.png" data-enlarge data-caption="The style picker lists compatible deck styles and the save, edit and detach actions."><img src="/assets/media/docs/animation-style-picker.png" alt="Flux Slides with four rectangles on the stage and the Style menu open in the Animation inspector, listing a deck style and the Save as new style, Edit style and Detach actions." width="1600" height="1000" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>The style picker lists compatible deck styles and the save, edit and detach actions. Click to enlarge.</figcaption></figure>

A local edit shows **override** beside **↺ use style**. Reset removes that field's override
so it follows the style again. Setting stagger to zero turns it off for this effect. Setting
both custom influence values to zero in the editor resets the timing field to its style or
preset default. A stored zero-influence record can explicitly suppress inherited influence,
but the editor’s zero action restores inheritance. **Edit style…** opens the shared
fields under an **Editing style ‹name› · N tracks** banner; **Back to effect** returns to local
edits. **Detach** keeps the current settings as independent values.

<figure class="doc-figure"><a href="/assets/media/docs/animation-style-override.png" data-enlarge data-caption="A linked effect with a duration override and its use-style reset."><img src="/assets/media/docs/animation-style-override.png" alt="The Animation inspector for an effect linked to a style. Its duration field is marked override, with a use style reset beside it." width="1600" height="1000" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>A linked effect with a duration override and its use-style reset. Click to enlarge.</figcaption></figure>

Right-click a timing bar and choose **Animate like…**, then click an object on the canvas.
The picker's outline and hover show which object you are on and name its effect in this step;
one click commits.
Its effect in this step supplies the style. If it has no style, Flux creates **Like ‹object
label›** and links both effects. A multi-selection links in bulk; incompatible families are
reported. In the X-ray, **6** arms the same pick for the selected objects or parts. **Esc** cancels.

In the animation **Library**, clicking a preset's name still applies a copy of it. Its
**as a linked style** action instead creates a deck style from that preset and links the
effects it is applied to. Slide presets include
the deck styles they use and restore their links when inserted.

### Follow timing {#follow-timing}

Hold **Ctrl/Cmd** and drag a bar's **left edge** onto another bar's start or end. The magnet
guide turns solid; releasing creates a timing anchor with zero offset. A link glyph marks the
follower. Retiming the source moves its followers live, including the source's stagger tail.
You can also choose **⛓ Follow timing…** in the inspector and select a lane's start or end.

<figure class="doc-figure"><a href="/assets/media/docs/animation-follow-timing.png" data-enlarge data-caption="The linked follower and the inspector’s after-lane-end row."><img src="/assets/media/docs/animation-follow-timing.png" alt="The Animator with a follower bar linked to the end of another bar. The inspector's start row reads after Lead end + 0 ms." width="1440" height="1000" loading="lazy"></a><figcaption>The linked follower and the inspector’s after-lane-end row. Click to enlarge.</figcaption></figure>

An anchored start row reads **after ‹lane› end + 0 ms** and displays the resolved start.
Its primary input edits the **offset**. Choose **⛓ Detach** to retain the resolved start as
absolute milliseconds. A plain bar drag also detaches and names the former lane in a toast;
one Undo restores the whole gesture. Missing targets, cross-step references and cycles show
the compiler's issue text with the stored start as fallback.

Animation styles and timing anchors are also available from the CLI and MCP, through
`anim-style`, `animate-like` and `set-track`:

```bash
flux anim-style create talk --name "Gentle reveal" --family appearance \
  --preset fade --duration 400
flux set-track talk slide1 effect1 --style STYLE_ID
flux animate-like talk slide1 --from effect1 --to effect2,effect3
flux set-track talk slide1 effect2 --anchor effect1:end:50
```

The last command starts effect2 50 ms after effect1 ends, including its stagger tail.
Retiming effect1 moves effect2 automatically. Anchors stay within one step; self-links and
cycles are refused. A removed anchor target leaves a visible issue and uses the follower's
stored start. `set-track --start` adjusts an anchored effect's offset; `--no-anchor` keeps its
current resolved start. `--no-style` detaches its style. A start cascade adjusts anchor offsets;
a duration cascade writes local overrides on linked effects.

Successive appearance effects follow the prior effect's end. [Auto-animate](#auto-animate)
links a plot's Data-phase geometry to the points' start, plus half of the original stagger delay.

### Playback and inspection {#playback-and-inspection}

**Step** plays only the selected step. **Play** starts from that step and continues through the slide;
**Slide** plays the whole slide. **Space** toggles play/pause and **Stop** returns to editing. The
playhead follows the actual player clock. Drag the ruler to inspect a precise time without editing
the document or changing the edit destination. Playback retains the last frame for inspection.
**Loop** repeats the chosen playback range. Editing a property cancels the old preview so the next
preview uses the updated document. Use Present for manual click-by-click rehearsal.

### Choose an effect {#appearances}

The Effect menu of the Animation inspector lists every appearance effect; the deck file and the
commands know them by the preset names in the second column.

| Effect | Preset | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| **Fade in** / **Fade out** | `fade` / `fadeOut` | Opacity rises from, or falls to, nothing |
| **Rise in** | `fadeRise` | Fades in while rising into place |
| **Pop in** / **Pop out** | `popIn` / `popOut` | Fades in while growing from 90 % of its size; fades out while shrinking to 92 % |
| **Scale in** / **Scale out** | `scaleIn` / `scaleOut` | Grows from nothing, and shrinks back to it, about a point: the centre, an arrow's tail, or the shared centre of the objects that appear together. Never fades. The default for rectangles, ellipses and arrows |
| **Grow bars** | `growBaseline` | Each bar grows from its own zero line: vertical bars up (down when negative), horizontal bars from the left (right when negative) |
| **Draw on** / **Draw off** | `drawOn` / `drawOff` | A pen traces the stroke; see [Draw like a pen](#draw-like-a-pen) |
| **Wipe in** / **Wipe out** | `writeOn` / `wipeOut` | Sweeps the text's own ink left to right, right to left, top to bottom or bottom to top, with no dead lead or tail (a rotated or flipped target sweeps its whole box). **Wipe edge** chooses **Soft**, a feathered leading edge on text, or **Hard**, the plain clip; new wipes are soft |
| **Stagger in** | `stagger` | Members of a group or points of a series arrive in sequence; see [Stagger order and spacing](#stagger) |
| **Highlight** | `highlight` | Dips to 40 % opacity and returns, easing into the dip from where the object is |
| **Dim** | `dim` | Lowers opacity to 30 % and stays there, starting from the object's current opacity |
| **Pulse** | `pulse` | Swells by 12–30 %, sized to the object and never past the slide edge, and returns. Emphasize's default |
| **Circle it** | `encircle` | Traces a rounded band round the object, or round a sentence's ink, and leaves nothing behind |
| **Count up** | `countUp` | Tweens a number in a text element ("n = 1,247" counts up in place). The digits stay put while counting, each in its place-value slot, for centred and right-aligned numbers too |

A new **Appear** writes Rise in for text, images and plots, Scale in for rectangles, ellipses and
arrows, and Draw on for lines and paths; **Disappear** writes their exits. Pop in and Highlight
remain, and saved decks keep playing as made. Pulse and Circle it add no PowerPoint slide. Scatter
points and axis ticks animate under Pop in, Rise in and Stagger in. Every effect starts and lands
without a pop: a draw grows from nothing, and text that glides lands on the crisp resting text.

#### Draw like a pen {#draw-like-a-pen}

Draw on and Draw off expose full **trim path** control: direction, anchor, single, both ends or
middle-out, and partial windows. A draw behaves like a pen. A filled shape traces its outline
first and fills as the pen comes round, an arrowhead grows out of the end of its shaft, a dashed
line draws dash by dash, and a dotted line draws solid and takes its dots when the draw ends. The
stroke finishes at about 94 % of the duration, so draws in older decks end about 100 ms later
than they used to.

A Draw on an axis's tick marks with no stagger set plays the ticks one by one along the axis, in
the pen's direction, in the same total time; set **Stagger → Each** to 0 ms to opt out.

**Trace strokes in order**, a toggle on a Draw, draws the strokes of an imported drawing with
several paths one after another at one pen speed, each weighted by its length (a Draw off takes
the last stroke first). Flux turns it on for such drawings, never for a plot.

#### Draw a line along x {#draw-along-x}

**Draw along x**, a toggle on the Draw of a plot's data line, draws the line at an even pace
along its x axis instead of along its length, so a steep stretch no longer rushes past. Its
confidence band, error bars and markers ride the same front, and **Lead dot** adds a dot at the
tip that exists only while it rides. [Auto-animate](#auto-animate) writes all of this for every
line series, and a fit line beside a scatter keeps drawing as the points arrive.

A line that doubles back in x, a step or ECDF line, a closed line or one that runs outside its
axes keeps drawing along its length, and a draw along x takes a curve that stays between its
ends (no spring, overshoot or steps). From the command line, for one series:

```bash
flux draw-along-x talk slide1 plot1 growth [--pen auto|on|off] [--duration 1400]
flux draw-along-x talk slide1 plot1 growth --off   # draw by length again; effects and timing stay
```

`--pen auto` adds the lead dot only when no markers ride along. `--off`, or unticking the box,
turns the x clock off and leaves the effects and their timing as they are.

<!-- MEDIA: A sine-like data line drawn by length (racing through its steep parts) beside the same line drawn along x with a lead dot, its band opening behind the front and markers growing in as it reaches them. -->

#### Stagger order and spacing {#stagger}

**By** sets the stagger order: **order** (target order), **x →** or **y ↑** (data position),
**value** (each part's own value — a hexagon's mean, a cell's value, a bar's height — low to
high), **count** (observations per hexagon), **data index** (the generator's index) or
**radial**. The order comes from the plot's data, so a hexmatrix can fill from its emptiest
hexagon to its fullest. **Radial** ranks a plot's points (or bars, hexagons, cells) by their
distance from the centre of the group, as it looks on screen: from **start** they ripple
outwards, from **end** they collapse inwards. A deck that uses it is saved in the newer format,
which older Flux versions do not open.

With **x →** or **y ↑** from the start or the end, **spacing** chooses **even** (one step per
item) or **true** (each item waits in proportion to its distance along the axis, so markers
that sit unevenly appear exactly as a line drawn along x reaches them).

Use **Stagger → Each** for the delay between ranks, or **Total** for the time between the
first and last item starting. Switching modes preserves the current span. **From → Random**
uses a repeatable order; edit **Seed** or click **↻** to reshuffle (one Undo restores it).
The distribution curve controls how densely starts fall within the span: an ease-out curve
starts widely spaced, then packs later starts together. Springs are clamped to the span.
Center and Edges keep symmetric pairs together; if every item ties, Total uses input order.
A single target has no stagger tail.

```bash
flux set-track talk slide1 effect1 --stagger-total 800 --stagger-curve enter \
  --stagger-from random --seed 42
flux set-track talk slide1 effect1 --stagger-each 30
flux set-track talk slide1 effect1 --stagger-each 30 --stagger-by count
flux set-track talk slide1 effect1 --stagger-each 40 --stagger-by x --stagger-spacing true
flux set-track talk slide1 effect1 --stagger-total 900 --stagger-by radial \
  --stagger-origin 2.5,1   # ripple out from (2.5, 1), in the plot's data units
```

`--stagger-origin` gives a radial order another centre, in the plot's data units; without it the
parts' own centre is used.

### Cascading tracks {#cascading-tracks}

Select several tracks and press **Ctrl+Alt+C** to open the same
[cascade](/docs/figure-layout.html#cascade) popover that Figure uses for layout. Here it steps
an animation value evenly across the selection: **start**, **duration**, **per-item or total
stagger**, **Arc**, easing **influence** or **Spring bounce**. Spring bounce skips effects
without a spring, and they do not use up a step. Five drawOn effects starting 120 ms apart
take one gesture instead of five edits.
